walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 1: Performing and Appraising — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 1: Performing and Appraising brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 1: Performing and Appraising.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many crotchets equal a semibreve?
A dot after a note adds?
options: A quarter of its value
A half of its value
A full extra
A double value

mcqs.q: How do you identify a major key from its key signature?
options: It is always C major.
The last sharp is the leading note (semitone below tonic); the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
The number of sharps or flats equals the tonic note number.
Classical means any old serious music.

mcqs.q: What is the function of the bridge in a pop song?
options: It is the very first section.
Classical means any old serious music.
To provide contrast before the final chorus, often by changing melody, key, or texture.
It is the same as the chorus.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes Classical (1750-1820) from Baroque style?
options: It is the very first section.
Classical means any old serious music.
Use of orchestra (Baroque had none).
Clearer melodic phrases, homophonic texture, balanced structures like sonata form.
